l: So, surrounding, let-us-seize, saying, word agreed-on-(object), Atan-of younger-brother Jeke-Čelen, own-home-to coming, saying:
i: Jeke-Chelen, Atan's younger brother, came back to his own home, and (told of) the word they had agreed on, "So let us surround and seize him," and said:
n: The first words are a back-reference: Tein bučižu barija keġen üge, 'the word that says "so, surrounding, let us seize"', and baralduγsan-i (Ming 商議定了的 行) is the participle 'what was agreed' with the accusative: the agreed word is what Jeke-Chelen carries home. Atan-u deġü is 'Atan's younger brother', possessor first. ger-tür(i)-jen is ger 'home' + dative-locative -tür + reflexive-possessive -(i)jen (Ming 家 自的行), 'to his own home'. irežü, 'coming', and ügülerün, 'saying', are the usual converbs. Who is to be seized is not said here; the next unit names Temüjin. Atan is a name known to the Ming only as 人名 'a man's name'; Jeke-Čelen is the Čelen of the published parts (the next unit's speaker; his brother's son is named below).

l: "Tomorrow early Temüžin-(object) let-us-seize," said-together.
i: "Tomorrow, early, let us seize Temüjin," they agreed.
n: manaγar erte is 'tomorrow, early' (Ming 明 早). Temüžin-i, with the accusative -i (Ming 行), is the object of barija, 'let us seize'. keġeldübe is keġe- 'say' + reciprocal -ldü- 'together' + past -be (Ming 共說了): 'they said it to each other', that is, agreed. The opening quotation mark is Shiratori's; the speech closes with the verb.

l: "This word Temüžin-to word bringing going person-(object) how only be-made?" saying-said.
i: "And who is to be the man to go and carry this word to Temüjin? How is it to be done?" he said.
n: A hard sentence; this is a first reading. Ene üge-ji Temüžin-e kelen kürgen odqu küġün-i is 'the man who is to go bringing this word to Temüjin': odqu is the participle 'one who goes' (Ming 去的), kürgen the converb 'bringing, delivering' (Ming 送), küġün-i the person as object (Ming 人行). The verb is bolγaγdaju, bol- 'become' + causative -γa- + passive -γda-, 'be made (to happen)' (Ming 被做有), and ambar … ele is 'how, only' (Ming 怎生 但). I take the question to be 'who will be made the messenger, how is it to be managed'; the stem and ending are uncertain. The verb keġe-žüġüi 'said' is split across the line break (keġe- / žüġüi). Whether this means Jeke-Chelen is already thinking of a spoken warning to Temüjin, or is asking how the party can deliver a challenge to him, is not clear; the Ming will not decide it.

l: So, saying-when, his wife Alaγčid saying:
i: When he had said this, his wife Alahchid said:
n: ügüleküi-dür is ügüle- 'speak' + participle -küi + dative-locative -dür, 'at the speaking, when he said' (Ming 說的 行); the pattern 'verb-küi-dür' means 'when', and is the one to look for. eme in-ü is 'his wife', the possessive in-ü standing after its noun (Ming 妻 他的). Alaγčid is Ming 人名 only; I take it to be a woman's name and her husband to be Jeke-Chelen.

l: "That rash word, your what is? People also true-be-let," had-said.
i: "That hasty talk of yours, what is it? Let people, too, be honest!" she said.
n: tere deleme üge is 'that rash word' (Ming 那 造次 言語); čin-u is 'your' (či 'you', genitive on the stem čin-), and jaγ̇un bolumui 'what is it?' (Ming 甚麽 做有). The last clause is a puzzle. haran ba ünemigeġüžei: haran 'people' (Ming 人), ba 'also' (Ming 也), and a verb ünemige- that I have drawn from the Ming 做眞誠 'be made sincere' with the optative-like ending -ġüžei. I take it as a warning that a plot cannot be kept from people: let people (also) be honest, that is, others will be true to their word and tell. This is the reading to hold lightly; the other is that she asks him to act honestly himself.

l: So, saying-when, horse-herder his Badai fresh-mare's-milk bringing coming, this this word hearing, turned-back.
i: While she was saying this, Badai, his horse-herder, who had come bringing mare's milk, heard these words and went back.
n: aduγ̇uči in-ü Badai is 'his horse-herder Badai' (aduγ̇uči 'horse-herder', Ming 放馬的; in-ü after its noun). sün is mare's milk (Ming 生馬妳子); kürgere irežü is 'bringing, coming' (Ming 送來 來着), a double converb. ene ene is printed twice in the source and glossed twice by the Ming (這 這); I keep the repetition in the words but say 'these words' once in the English. keleleküi-dür is again 'when (he/she) said' (the verb here is kele- 'speak', from kele 'tongue'); it is not stated whether this refers to Jeke-Chelen or his wife.

l: Badai going, companion horse-herder Kišiliγ-to, Čeren-of said words spoke.
i: Badai went and told Kishiliq, his fellow horse-herder, the words Cheren had spoken.
n: nökör aduγ̇uči Kišiliγ-a is 'to the companion (and) horse-herder Kishiliq' (Ming 伴當 放馬的; -a is the dative-locative, Ming 行). Čeren-ü ügülegsen üges is 'the words said by Cheren', ügülegsen the past participle (Ming 說了的) and üges the plural (Ming 言語每). The speaker is called Čeren here and Jeke-Čelen in the first unit; the Ming has 人名 beside each. I treat Čelen and Čeren as one man, the Jeke-Čeren of unit 19 below; Shiratori's printing (l / r) is kept.

l: Kišiliγ saying: "I again going, let-me-find-out," saying, home-to went.
i: Kishiliq said, "I will go again and find out," and went to the tent.
n: Bi basa odču is 'I, again, going' (Ming 我 再 去着). uqasuγai is uqa- 'understand' (stem drawn from the Ming 察聽 'inquire, listen') + an optative -suγai, 'let me find out' (Ming 咱). ger-tür 'to the tent' is the same ger-tür as unit 1, here without the possessive. odčuγ̇ui is od- 'go' + past -čuγ̇ui (Ming 去了). Where he goes is the home of Cheren, to hear for himself.

l: Čeren-of son Narin-Keġen outside sitting, own-arrows polishing sitting, saying:
i: Cheren's son Narin-Kegen was sitting outside, sitting there polishing his arrows, and said:
n: Čeren-ü köġün Narin-Keġen is 'Cheren's son Narin-Kegen' (possessor first). γada saγ̇užu is 'outside, sitting' (Ming 外面 坐着), and sumud(i)-jan hürün saγ̇užu 'sitting, whetting his own arrows' (Ming 箭 自的行 磋 坐着): sumud is the plural of sumu 'arrow', -(i)jan the reflexive-possessive, 'his own'. hürün is hürü- (stem drawn from the Ming 磋 'to grind') + converb -n. The doubled saγ̇užu is as printed.

l: "Just-now we what said-together? Own-speech to-be-taken, whose mouth to-be-stopped?" had-said.
i: "What have we just been saying to one another? Our words are being taken up; whose mouth can be stopped?" he said.
n: tuγar bida jaγ̇u keġeldüleġei is 'just now we, what, said together' (Ming 恰纔 咱 甚 共說來): bida is the inclusive 'we' (Ming 咱), and -leġei the past (Ming 來). kele-ben abdaqun is 'own speech (is) to be taken' (Ming 話 自的行 被取的): ab- 'take' + passive -da- + the ending -qun. ken-ü ama idqaqun is 'whose mouth (is) to be stopped' (Ming 誰的 口 止當的), idqa- being 'stop, check'. Narin-Kegen has seen Badai leave and fears the words are out. The endings -qun are unsettled; I read both as 'will be', with the question carried by the sentence.

l: So said-having, Narin-Keġen again his-own-horse-herder Kišiliγ-to saying:
i: Having said that, Narin-Kegen spoke again to Kishiliq, his own horse-herder:
n: kēġed is keġe- 'say' + converb -ġed, written together with the stem and a long ē (Ming 說了). aduγ̇uči-daγ̇dan is 'to his own horse-herder' (Ming 放馬的 自的行): I read -daγ̇dan as the dative-locative with a reflexive-possessive; the ending is uncertain. Kišiliγ-a is the dative-locative again. That Narin-Kegen speaks to Kishiliq, who has just been listening at his tent, is the Ming's reading (人名行 'to the man named').

l: "Merkidai-Čaγaγan, Aman-Čaγaγan-Keġer two-(object) seizing bring. Tie. Night early I-mount," had-said.
i: "Seize the two horses Merkidai-Chagan and Aman-Chagan-Keger and bring them. Tie them up. I shall ride early in the night," he said.
n: The two horse-names are Ming 馬名 'a horse's name'; Aman-Čaγaγ̇an-Keġer is split over a line (Aman-Čaγaγ̇an- / Keġer). qojar-i is 'the two' with accusative -i (Ming 兩箇行). barižu abčira is 'seizing, bring!' (Ming 拿有 將來), where abčira is a bare stem, the imperative; hujažu is 'tying' with the imperative sense (Ming 拴着). süni erte morilaqu: 'night, early, I mount' (Ming 夜裏 早 上馬我), morila- being 'mount a horse' (mori 'horse') + the participle -qu. 'Early in the night' is my rendering of süni erte; it could be 'at night, early (before dawn)'. The two horses are named white (čaγaγan, 'Chagan') ones; whether Aman-Chagan-Keger's keġer is 'steppe' is not said.

l: Kišiliγ going, Badai-to saying: "Just-now-of word your was-verified, truly became.
i: Kishiliq went to Badai and said, "What you said just now has been verified; it has truly come about.
n: Kišiliγ jorčižu Badai-(j)a ügülerün: the speech is split ügü- / lerün across a line, ügü-lerün 'saying'. tuγar-un kelen čin-u is 'just-now's word, your (word)': tuγar-un is tuγar 'just now' with a genitive (Ming 恰纔), čin-u is 'your'. bolγaγ̇aba is a form I cannot parse closely: bol- 'become' with a causative and the past -ba, 'was made true' (Ming 體覆了 'checked, verified'). maγad bolba is 'truly became' (Ming 實 做了). The sense is that Badai's report is confirmed by what Kishiliq has seen. This is a first reading of the verb.

l: Now we two Temüžin-to word bringing, let-us-go," saying, word
i: Now let the two of us go and take word to Temüjin," he said, and the word (of that)
n: edöġe bida qojar 'now we two' (Ming 如今 咱 兩箇); Temüžin-e kelen kürgen jorčija 'to Temüjin, the word, bringing, let us go' (Ming 送去咱). jorčija is jorči- 'go' + -ja 'let us', the same ending as barija. keġen üge: 'saying, the word', which closes the quotation and leads into the next unit: the construction 'saying the word, agreeing' continues in baraldužu. I keep it as one thought across the two units; the English runs on.

l: agreeing, Merkidai-Čaγaγan, Aman-Čaγaγan-Keġer two-(object) seizing coming, tying,
i: agreed on it. Then, seizing the horses Merkidai-Chagan and Aman-Chagan-Keger and bringing them, they tied them up,
n: baraldužu is baraldu- 'settle together' (stem inferred from Ming 議定) + converb -žu: 'agreeing'. The sentence goes on through the converb chain barižu irežü hujažu 'seizing, coming, tying' (Ming 拿着 來着 拴着); I cut the chain here and again at 'evening' because it runs nine converbs. The horse names are as in unit 11; the accusative qojar-i again marks 'the two'. Whose horses they are is not said: they are the ones Narin-Kegen named.

l: Evening then own-tent-in one lamb killing, own-spit-with cooking-through,
i: In the evening they killed a lamb in their own tent and cooked it through on its spit,
n: üdeši büġed is 'evening, then' (Ming 晩夕 便), büġed being a particle that marks the next step. qos-tur(i)-jan is 'in their own tent' (Ming 房子 自的行): qos is my guess for the head, 'house, tent'. nigen quriγa-ban alažu is 'one lamb (their own), killing' (Ming 一箇 羔兒 殺着), quriγa-ban with the reflexive-possessive. iseri-jer-en bolγažu: iseri is Ming 床 'bed, frame', jer- the instrumental 'with', and bolγažu 'making become' = 'cooking through' (Ming 煮熟着). 'On its spit' is a guess at what a 床 for cooking might be; the Ming word is bed or frame and I do not know what object is meant.

l: Merkidai-Čaγaγan, Aman-Čaγaγan-Keġer two ready tied-ones riding, by-night going,
i: then mounted the two horses, Merkidai-Chagan and Aman-Chagan-Keger, that they had kept ready tied, and rode off by night,
n: The first horse-name is split across the line (Merkidai- / Čaγaγ̇an). belen is Ming 見 'seen' and I read it as 'ready, at hand'; hujaγsad-i is 'the ones that were tied' with the plural past participle -γsad and the accusative -i (Ming 拴着的 行). unužu 'riding' (Ming 騎着), süni-de 'by night' (dative-locative, Ming 夜裏 行 as in the published parts), jorčižu 'going'. The horses stay the same pair as in the two instructions.

l: Čiṅgis Qaγan-to night arriving, tent-of from-behind Badai, Kišiliγ two saying:
i: They reached Chinggis Qahan in the night, and from behind his tent Badai and Kishiliq said:
n: Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur is 'to Chinggis Qaγan' (Ming 太祖 皇帝行), the dative-locative -dur with the title in the form of the published parts. süni kürčü is 'by night, arriving' (Ming 夜裏 到着). ger-ün ümerēče is 'from behind the tent' (Ming 房的 北處): ger-ün is the genitive 'of the tent', ümer 'behind' with the ablative -ēče. The two men speak from behind the tent, unseen. The subject of kürčü is the two herdsmen; their coming together is the Ming's (兩箇 'the two').

l: "Jeke-Čeren-of said words, son-(object) his Narin-Keġen-of arrows polishing sitting said-(object), Merkidai-Čaγaγan, Aman-Čaγaγan-Keġer two geldings seizing tie said words, all-(object) saying gave.
i: "The words that Jeke-Cheren spoke, and what his son Narin-Kegen said as he sat polishing his arrows, namely, 'Seize the two geldings Merkidai-Chagan and Aman-Chagan-Keger and tie them up,' the words that were said, all of them they told.
n: A long sentence, cut here and carried by its quotation. Jeke-Čeren-ü ügülegsen üges is 'the words that Jeke-Cheren spoke'; köġün-i in-ü Narin-Keġen-(n)ü … ügülegsen-i 'what his son Narin-Kegen said' (Ming 子 行 他的 人名的 … 說來的 行), with the accusative -i on the participle; -(n)ü after an n-final stem is the front-vowel form, breaking harmony as the published parts do. aγtas is 'geldings' (Ming 騸馬每), the plural of aγta, huja 'tie!' (Ming 拴), keġegsen üges 'the words said' (Ming 說來的 言語每), bügüde-ji 'all (object)' (Ming 都 行), ügüležü ögbe 'telling, gave' (Ming 說着 與了). The Ming reads the horses as geldings here, not as the named pair of unit 11; they are the same two. The unit's quotation marks do not close, as in the source.

l: Again Badai, Kišiliγ two saying:
i: Badai and Kishiliq then said again:
n: basa 'again' (Ming 再), qojar 'the two' after the pair (Ming 兩箇), ügülerün 'saying': the pattern that opens each speech.

l: "Čiṅgis Qaγan-(object) if-favour, doubt there-is-not.
i: "If Chinggis Qahan will show favour (to what we say), there is no doubt.
n: sojurγaγ̇asu is sojurγa- 'show favour, bestow a grace' (Ming 恩賜) + conditional -γ̇asu (Ming 呵), 'if (he) favours'. The word before it is Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-i with the accusative -i (Ming 皇帝行), so the grammar reads 'if (one) favours Chinggis Qahan', not 'if Chinggis Qahan favours'. I give the sense the Ming points to, that favour is looked for from him; the subject of the favour is not named. arijal ügei bi is 'doubt there is not' (Ming 疑 無 有): the speakers claim certainty. A doubtful sentence; the note leans on the Ming only.

l: Surrounding, let-us-seize, saying, word agreed," said.
i: Surrounding him, let us seize him' — that is the word they agreed on," they said.
n: The unit returns to the words of the first one: bučižü barija keġen üge, 'the word saying "surrounding, let us seize"', and baralduba 'agreed' (Ming 共議定了). The structure closes the section, as it opened it, on the agreed plot; keġebe 'said' (Ming 說了) ends the whole of §169. Where the English quotation begins is unclear because Shiratori's marks (opening before Čiṅgis at word 193, closing after baralduba at word 203) enclose the whole speech.
